newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower as China conflict cited.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower as China conflict cited.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on commercial and fund selling and a trade conflict with China was cited, traders said.
"There were fears hanging over the market on China's retaliation but the perceptions are, nothing will come of it," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
China said it expected talks with the United States soon on a dispute over U.S. sanctions on its textiles and its own threat to retaliate.
The commercial selling in soybeans helped magnify the China talk but technical selling was evident, they said.
Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp and Cargill Inc were key sellers on the day and Cargill was a late seller of one million bushels, traders said.
Technicians cited first support in the November at $6.84-1/2 a bushel and second support at $6.79. The session low for November was $6.79.
Position squaring was noted before the release at 0730 CST Tuesday of USDA's November crop production and supply/demand reports.
Soybeans closed four to eight cents per bushel lower, with November down 7-3/4 at $6.80.
An average of analysts' estimates ahead of the USDA reports, pegged the 1996 U.S. soybean crop at 2.376 billion bushels.
Traders also cited the potential for further long liquidation after the release Friday of an updated Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report.
CFTC said as of November 5, funds were long soybeans by roughly 1.3 to 1.0 ratio.
Declines were curbed by recent active soy exports, strong U.S. soybean crush paces and slow farmer selling, traders said.
Also another day of strong stopping of the deliveries posted against the November contract was supportive. ADM Investor Services stopped 100,000 of the 105,000 posted, CBOT said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 40,000 contracts, below the 47,681 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Refco Inc bought 200 January $7.00 calls at 12-1/2 to 12-3/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, above the 15,392 traded Friday, CBOT said.
